checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: A versioned policy defines cumulative Lite, Standard, and Strict calibration controls; Lite contains source paths, test paths, generated paths, protected paths, quality command, default branch, project owner, reviewer, and major unknowns while excluding Strict-only controls.

Calibration Profile validation requires level, human selection evidence, timestamp, reasons, exact required controls, and exact deferred controls, and fails closed for unknown levels, malformed policy, missing evidence, or control drift.

Profile transitions allow Lite to Standard and Standard to Strict without exception evidence; any downgrade requires original level, new level, reason, closed controls, risk acceptor, and effective scope, and rejects incomplete or falsely declared transition records.
Generated calibration proposals and the confirmed template Project Profile expose a valid calibrationProfile while existing legacy version 1 profiles without that section remain readable.

The validator and Make entrypoint are installed into adopter repositories, and focused tests cover all levels, upgrade, downgrade, invalid policy, legacy compatibility, proposal rendering, and installation parity.

English, Japanese, and Simplified Chinese reference documentation state required/deferred controls, evidence limits, transition recovery, and non-claims without expanding AI Cockpit beyond Repository Governance Layer.
guidelines: New public APIs must be documented.
Do not import internal modules from other features.

intent.problem: Calibration currently presents one heavy control surface, so ordinary and first-time adopters can be forced to supply release-grade evidence that is unrelated to their current risk. The repository needs explicit Lite, Standard, and Strict calibration levels whose requirements are deterministic and reviewable.
constraints: Preserve Evidence over Self-Declaration and fail closed on malformed or incomplete profile evidence.
Lite must not require supply-chain, release attestation, dual-person activation, enterprise audit, or external identity evidence.
Profiles may upgrade monotonically; downgrade requires an explicit bounded risk-acceptance record.
Preserve existing Project Profile compatibility and the current calibration session lifecycle.
Do not implement WI06 capability-claim binding or WI08 installer UX in this Work Item.
intent.rationale: A single policy-backed validator and persisted profile selection makes calibration proportional without weakening high-risk controls or duplicating the existing session and quality-routing authorities.

rawUserRequest: Execute WI-05 Calibration Profiles from the provided next-stage development directive: add Lite, Standard, and Strict calibration levels, keep Lite lightweight, make requirements cumulative, allow upgrades, require a complete recorded exception for downgrades, and complete the full branch, PR, merge, archive, and cleanup lifecycle.
